text:
sophia: Heads-up: we're launching a new "Traffic Smoothing (velocity)" policy next week to reduce spike-driven overages and protect latency for everyone. It adds a 60s rolling throughput check that can trigger short automatic pacing windows when sustained token rate exceeds configured capacity. Draft policy + FAQ: https://redwood.internal/policies/traffic-smoothing

maria: Is this a replacement for per-second rate limits or an additional layer? Will customers receive 429s?

sophia: It's additive. Per-second limits remain. The smoothing layer is meant to prevent very bursty traffic from causing systemic latency issues. Most cases will result in a brief pacing period (usually <= 30s) rather than immediate 429 responses. Hard throttles only on repeated breaches or correlated errors.

darren: How will Dedicated (reserved) customers be treated versus hosted pay-as-you-go?

sophia: Dedicated respects reserved capacity and pool config; velocity actions are much less likely there unless the burst pattern is extreme across the pool. Hosted customers may see more holdbacks during large spikes. We'll provide a per-account dashboard toggle for aggressiveness.

els: Any billing changes? If requests are delayed by pacing, are tokens still billed?

sophia: Billing is unchanged: tokens that complete are billed as usual. Pacing prevents additional token generation during the hold window. Finance will publish edge-case guidance and an auto-rebate flow for confirmed system-induced failures.

finance-bot: Note: automated rebate flow will trigger for verified system-side pacing events that caused failed completions. See finance FAQ once published.

allison: We need a clear customer message. "Debit holdback" sounds scary.

sophia: Agreed. Public wording will use "traffic smoothing" or "temporary request pacing". Proposed blurb: "To keep latency predictable, we may briefly pace very large bursts of requests. This helps avoid elevated latency and service interruptions."

support: Updating support runbook now with troubleshooting steps: how to check velocity charts, verify X-Redwood-Velocity header, escalate if persistent. ETA: EOD.

maria: Mitigation advice for customers? Client retry/backoff guidance?

sophia: Recommend exponential backoff with jitter (start ~500ms, cap ~2s), prefer idempotent design, and detect header X-Redwood-Velocity-Hold: true to avoid hammering. We'll add SDK helpers.

darren: Can we include a curl example for detecting the header?

sophia: Yes. Example to include in KB:

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
# check response headers for: X-Redwood-Velocity-Hold: true
```

eli: Rollout plan?

sophia: Staged rollout Monday 09:00 PT: 10% hosts -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours if no anomalies. Auto-abort on SLO regressions: p99 latency > +5% or error rate spike.

allison: Comms timeline: pre-notify top accounts Tue AM, blog + docs Wed, in-console banner Wed PM. Support and CSMs will have scripts.

support: Playbook pushed to support runbook. Adding KB article and canned responses.

ops-bot: Canary vel-2026-02 started. Dashboards: velocity_rate, pacing_events_per_min, p99_latency.

maria: Please ping #customer-ops before blog goes live so CS can prep priority customers.

sophia: Will do. TL;DR: introducing traffic smoothing (1m velocity), brief pacing windows possible, header + backoff guidance, staged rollout Mon. Feedback welcome. :rocket:
